svg.title: Motor to Gearbox to Wheel
svg.desc: A RoboLore instructional graphic explaining how twelve encoder counts per motor turn become 909.7 counts per wheel turn through a 75.81 to 1 gearbox. The wheel illustration has been updated to match the clearer white Zumo track wheel style used elsewhere in the book.
svg.text: The encoder is on the motor. The wheel is on the far side of a gearbox.
“The encoder gives 12 counts per rotation, so 12 counts = one wheel turn.”
No. 12 counts is one turn of the MOTOR SHAFT — and the motor spins 75.81 times
for every ONE turn of the wheel.
Zumo 32U4 robots ship with three different gearboxes. This lesson assumes the standard 75:1.
If yours is a 50:1 or a 100:1, EVERY number downstream of this graphic is wrong for your robot
— and it will be wrong in a way that looks like a code bug.
Check the box the robot came in before you spend an hour blaming your loop.
